tier_reason: The README's only number is 'up to 60x faster than the CPU', and it names no CPU renderer, scene, hardware or method. The repo has no benchmark code or result files: TestFiles/ holds only SVG and PDF test scenes, and the 4 issues hold no performance data. With no named baseline and no measurement behind the claim, it is directional only, so D.

corrections.baseline: unnamed CPU path rasterization ('the CPU'); the README names no CPU renderer. HN thread snippets (seen through search only) say the author used CoreGraphics as the quality reference and called performance against Vello 'very competitive', with no numbers.
corrections.license: Custom 'personal use zlib license' (LICENSE.txt): zlib terms, but permission is granted only for personal use, and commercial use needs a licence from the author. Not OSI-approved.
corrections.caveats: The only number is the unqualified 'up to 60x faster than the CPU'. It names no baseline library, scene, hardware or flags, and the repo has no benchmark code or results: TestFiles/ is SVG/PDF scenes only and the issues have no performance data. The HN thread 'Rasterizer: A GPU-accelerated 2D vector graphics engine in ~4k LOC' (item 45090553) was seen only as search snippets. They say 50,000 glyphs at 60fps (no hardware and no baseline), CoreGraphics as the quality reference, and Vello 'very competitive', with Rasterizer 'suspected' faster on complex scenes. None of these has a number against a named baseline. The licence is zlib-style but limited to personal use (commercial licence from the author), so it is not OSI-approved. It is macOS/Metal only (an iOS target was added in 2026), and the Xcode demo depends on bundled PDFium, NanoSVG, stb_truetype and xxHash. The ~4k LOC figure comes from the HN title and was not checked in the repo.
